zones.description: Residential quarters with perimeter blocks and semi-private courtyards located outside flood-prone riverfront zones, ensuring high-quality housing and visual permeability toward the Moskva River.
Higher-density mixed-use buildings along the Marc Chagall embankment integrate housing, grocery stores, cafés, and local services with active public waterfront spaces.
Flexible office campuses, technology hubs, coworking spaces, and research facilities support employment generation and reinforce the mixed-use redevelopment strategy.
Expansion of the existing Ice Palace and public event facilities with museums, exhibition spaces, sports halls, cinemas, and recreational programs connected to Tyufeleva Roshcha Park.
Schools, multiple kindergartens, healthcare centers, libraries, and community hubs distributed within walking distance of all residential sectors.
Continuous green corridors extending Tyufeleva Roshcha Park with ecological planting, playgrounds, sports fields, rainwater management landscapes, and pedestrian/cycling routes.
Public embankment with promenades, piers, terraces, cycling lanes, water recreation zones, and viewing decks preserving visual and physical access to the Moskva River.
Transport hubs, structured parking, service roads, and landscaped acoustic barriers along the Third Ring Road and railway mitigate traffic noise and improve multimodal accessibility.
Preserved historic industrial structures adapted into creative industries, workshops, galleries, educational spaces, and small-scale production facilities.

facts: Maximum building height does not exceed 15 floors.
Green and open public spaces occupy significantly more than the required 15% of the territory.
Residential buildings are excluded from flood risk zones along the Moskva River shoreline.
Visual corridors toward the Moskva River are preserved through stepped building placement and open public spaces.
Noise mitigation measures are concentrated along the Third Ring Road and railway boundary through landscaped buffers and building orientation.
The redevelopment includes multiple kindergartens and grocery stores within walking distance of residential blocks.
The Marc Chagall embankment functions as the primary public waterfront spine of the district.
The zoning structure integrates with MCC station ZIL, Tekhnopark metro station, and the planned ZIL metro station.
Historic industrial buildings are preserved and adaptively reused as cultural and creative facilities.
Tyufeleva Roshcha Park is integrated into a larger continuous ecological and recreational network.
